questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: The Post Correspondence Problem (PCP) over a binary alphabet `{0, 1}` is:
questions.explanationEn: A TM can systematically search all finite index sequences and halt-accept if a match exists (making PCP RE), but no algorithm can decide in general whether a match exists (undecidable).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following transformations preserve the language `L(G)` of a CFG (assuming `ε ∉ L(G)`)?
optionsEn: Converting G to Chomsky Normal Form
questions.explanationEn: All four are standard equivalence-preserving grammar simplification steps when `ε ∉ L(G)`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: For the ambiguous grammar `E -> E + E | a`, how many distinct parse trees exist for the string `a + a + a + a`?
questions.explanationEn: Each parse tree corresponds to a full parenthesization of 4 operands (3 binary `+` operators), counted by the Catalan number `C_3 = 5`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Context-Free Languages (CFLs) are CLOSED under which of the following operations?
questions.explanationEn: CFLs are NOT closed under intersection or complementation in general, but the intersection of a CFL with a Regular language is always a CFL (via product construction of a PDA and a DFA).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: How many strings of length 4 are generated by the regular expression `(ab + ba)*`?
questions.explanationEn: Strings of length 4 are concatenations of two 2-letter blocks from `{ab, ba}`: `abab, abba, baab, baba` — `2^2 = 4` strings.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Given a CFG in Chomsky Normal Form, what is the worst-case time complexity of the CYK (Cocke-Younger-Kasami) membership algorithm for an input string of length `n`?
questions.explanationEn: CYK fills an `n × n` upper-triangular dynamic programming table where each cell checks up to `n` split points, taking `O(n^3)` time (for a fixed grammar).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following decision problems are DECIDABLE?
optionsEn: Given a DFA M and a string w, does M accept w?
Given a CFG G, is L(G) infinite?
Given a Turing Machine M, does M halt on empty input ε?
Given a Regular Expression R, is L(R) = ∅?
questions.explanationEn: DFA membership (A), CFG finiteness/infiniteness (B), and regex emptiness (D) are all decidable. The blank-tape Halting Problem for TMs is undecidable (C is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over `Σ = {a, b}` that accepts all strings of length divisible by 4?
questions.explanationEn: The DFA cycles through 4 states corresponding to `|w| mod 4 ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3}`, with state 0 accepting. Minimum = 4 states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: A language `L` is Recursive (Decidable) if and only if:
optionsEn: Both L and its complement L' are Recursively Enumerable (RE)
L is RE and L' is Context-Free
L is accepted by a deterministic PDA
questions.explanationEn: By Post's Theorem, if both `L` and `L'` are RE, we can run their two semi-deciders in parallel (dovetailing); one must eventually halt, deciding membership in `L`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following regular expression identities hold for all regular expressions `R` and `S`?
questions.explanationEn: A, B, and C are classical Kleene algebra identities. D is false because `(a + b)*` contains `ab`, which is not in `a* + b*`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the CFG `S -> aS | bS | ε`. How many strings of length 6 over `{a, b}` are generated by this grammar?
questions.explanationEn: This grammar generates all strings `{a, b}*`, so there are `2^6 = 64` strings of length 6.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Consider the CFG: `S -> aSb | bSa | SS | ε`. What language over `{a, b}` does this grammar generate?
optionsEn: All strings with an equal number of 'a's and 'b's
All strings of the form a^n b^n
questions.explanationEn: Every production adds one `a` and one `b` (or concatenates two balanced strings), preserving `#a(w) = #b(w)`. Conversely, any non-empty string with equal `a`s and `b`s either starts and ends with opposite symbols (`aSb`/`bSa`) or splits into two non-empty balanced prefixes (`SS`).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following problems about an arbitrary Turing Machine `M` is DECIDABLE?
optionsEn: Does L(M) contain at least 10 strings?
Does M accept its own encoding <M>?
Does M make at least 10 moves when run on empty input ε?
questions.explanationEn: Simulating `M` on `ε` for up to 10 steps always terminates in finite time, so C is decidable (it is a bounded execution property, not a semantic language property). A, B, and D are all undecidable by Rice's Theorem / diagonalization.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following languages are Recursively Enumerable (RE) but NOT Recursive (Decidable)?
optionsEn: L1 = {<M, w> | TM M halts on input w}
L4 = {<M> | M accepts at least two distinct strings}
questions.explanationEn: For L1, simulate `M` on `w` and accept if it halts. For L2 and L4, dovetail `M` across all strings and accept once 1 (or 2) strings are accepted. All three are RE but undecidable. L3 is co-RE and NOT RE (C is false).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: What is the minimum number of states in a DFA over `{a}` (unary alphabet) that accepts `{a^n | n is divisible by 2 OR n is divisible by 3}`?
questions.explanationEn: The acceptance pattern repeats with period `lcm(2, 3) = 6`: residues `0, 2, 3, 4` accept and `1, 5` reject. Checking all 6 cyclic shifts shows no smaller period exists, so minimum = 6 states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.topicTag: TOC — Strings of Length 5 in CFL
questions.questionTextEn: How many strings of length 5 over `{a, b}` belong to the palindrome language `L = {w ∈ {a, b}* | w = w^R}`?
questions.explanationEn: A palindrome of length 5 is uniquely determined by its first 3 characters (positions 1, 2, 3), giving `2^3 = 8` strings.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: An NFA over `{0, 1}` has states `{q0, q1, q2}` with start state `q0`, accepting state `q2`, and transitions: `δ(q0, 0) = {q0, q1}`, `δ(q0, 1) = {q0}`, `δ(q1, 1) = {q2}`. Which language does this NFA accept?
questions.explanationEn: Since `q2` has no outgoing transitions, any accepting run must stay in `q0` until the second-to-last symbol (`0`), move to `q1`, and then read the final symbol (`1`) to reach `q2`. Thus it accepts all strings ending with `"01"`.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: If `L = {aa, aaa}`, what is the largest integer `n` such that `a^n ∉ L*` (the Frobenius number of 2 and 3)?
questions.explanationEn: By the Chicken McNugget theorem for coprime `a=2, b=3`, the largest unrepresentable integer is `ab - a - b = 6 - 2 - 3 = 1` (`a^0 = ε ∈ L*`, `a^1 ∉ L*`, and every `n >= 2` is achievable).

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.topicTag: TOC — NFA to DFA Subset Construction
questions.questionTextEn: Consider an NFA over `{a}` with states `{q0, q1, q2}` where `q0` is start, `q2` is accepting, and `δ(q0, a) = {q0, q1}`, `δ(q1, a) = {q2}`, `δ(q2, a) = ∅`. How many reachable states are in the DFA obtained by subset construction?
questions.explanationEn: Start: `{q0}`. On `a`: `{q0, q1}`. On `a`: `{q0, q1, q2}`. On `a`: `{q0, q1, q2}` (self-loop). Thus there are 3 reachable DFA states.

questions.pyqTag: GATE CS Topic • Theory of Computation (Set 2)
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following sets are COUNTABLY INFINITE?
optionsEn: The set of all valid C programs
The set of all Turing Machines
The set of all Regular languages over {0, 1}
The set of all languages over {0, 1} that are NOT Recursively Enumerable
questions.explanationEn: C programs, TMs, and Regular expressions/DFAs are all finite strings over a finite alphabet, hence countably infinite (A, B, C). Since all languages are uncountable and RE languages are countable, non-RE languages are uncountable (D is false).
